name: Container Escape to SPIRE Socket
description: Escape container isolation to access the host-level SPIRE Agent socket and harvest workload SVIDs — the canonical cross-domain attack chain combining container escape with SPIFFE identity theft
real_world_relevance: This is the highest-impact SPIFFE/SPIRE attack scenario. In real Kubernetes deployments, the SPIRE Agent runs as a DaemonSet with the Workload API socket mounted into pods. A container escape (via privileged container, hostPID, or kernel exploit) grants access to the host-level socket, enabling the attacker to harvest SVIDs for every workload on the node. Demonstrated by Eviatar Gerzi as the 'Spooffe' attack chain.

attack_flow.description: Attacker escapes from a privileged container using nsenter to access the host PID namespace, locates the SPIRE Agent socket on the host filesystem, and harvests X.509 SVIDs for all workloads running on the same node
diagram: 1. From privileged container, use nsenter to enter host PID/mount namespaces
2. Discover SPIRE Agent socket on the host filesystem
3. Verify socket accessibility and identify the SPIRE Agent process
4. Connect to the Workload API socket and fetch X.509 SVIDs
5. Harvest certificates and private keys for all node-local workloads
6. Use stolen SVIDs to establish mTLS connections as impersonated workloads

actions.description: Fetch X.509 SVIDs from host-level SPIRE socket — returns all workload identities on this node

actions.command: nsenter --target 1 --mount -- /bin/sh -c 'ls -la /tmp/escaped-svids/ 2>/dev/null && for f in /tmp/escaped-svids/svid.*.pem; do openssl x509 -in "$f" -noout -subject 2>/dev/null; done'
actions.description: List harvested SVIDs and extract SPIFFE IDs from certificate subjects

phases.name: Identity Impersonation
phases.description: Use harvested SVIDs to impersonate a workload via mTLS

actions.command: nsenter --target 1 --mount -- /bin/sh -c 'curl --cert /tmp/escaped-svids/svid.0.pem --key /tmp/escaped-svids/svid.0.key --cacert /tmp/escaped-svids/bundle.0.pem https://payment-service.internal:8443/api/transactions 2>/dev/null || echo "mTLS impersonation attempted with stolen SVID"'
actions.description: Attempt mTLS connection to internal service using stolen X.509 SVID

indicators_of_compromise.description: nsenter executed with namespace flags — container escape detected
SPIRE Workload API socket accessed from non-standard process context
Container escape followed by SPIRE socket access within 5 minutes — active attack chain

expected_wazuh_alerts.description: NHI: Container escape via nsenter namespace entry
NHI: SPIRE Workload API socket access detected
NHI-SPIRE: Container escape chain leading to SVID theft - ACTIVE ATTACK

immediate: Isolate the compromised node immediately — cordon and drain in Kubernetes
Revoke all SVIDs issued to workloads on the affected node
Force re-attestation of the SPIRE Agent on the node
Investigate how the container obtained privileged access (hostPID, privileged securityContext, CAP_SYS_ADMIN)
long_term: Enforce Pod Security Standards (Restricted profile) to prevent privileged containers and hostPID access
Use Kubernetes admission controllers (OPA Gatekeeper, Kyverno) to block nsenter, chroot, and mount namespace capabilities
Restrict SPIRE Agent socket permissions and use projected volumes instead of hostPath mounts
Deploy Falco or Tetragon for real-time container escape detection at the kernel level
Implement node attestation rotation — compromised nodes should fail re-attestation
Consider SPIRE Agent running in a hardened init container rather than as a DaemonSet with host access
